title: Geometric reducedness of local rings is invariant under field base change
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $L/k$ a field extension [def-pc-field-extension], $R$ a commutative $k$-algebra, and $S=R\otimes_kL$, with multiplication $(r\otimes a)(s\otimes b)=rs\otimes ab$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Let $\mathfrak q\subset S$ be a prime ideal and $\mathfrak p=\{r\in R:r\otimes1\in\mathfrak q\}$. Set $A=R_{\mathfrak p}$ and $B=S_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Then the following are equivalent: (1) for every field extension $E/k$ the ring $A\otimes_kE$ is reduced; (2) for every field extension $H/L$ the ring $B\otimes_LH$ is reduced. Here reduced means that every nilpotent element is zero. No finite type, Noetherian, algebraicity, or closed-point hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0384 (lemma-geometrically-reduced-upstairs), equivalence at x and x′, expressed in terms of local rings by Tag 035W (lemma-geometrically-reduced-at-point).

proof.text: Assume (1) and take any extension $H/L$. Write $V=R\setminus\mathfrak p$ and $U=S\setminus\mathfrak q$. Every $v\otimes1$ with $v\in V$ belongs to $U$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-cancel-base-change], first $A\otimes_kH$ is the localization of $R\otimes_kH$ at the images of $V$, and $B\otimes_LH$ is its further localization at the images of $U$. The cancellation isomorphism sends $h\otimes(r\otimes l)$ to $r\otimes hl$, with inverse $r\otimes h\mapsto h\otimes(r\otimes1)$; swapping factors gives the displayed order. Condition (1), applied to $H/k$, makes $A\otimes_kH$ reduced. A localization of a reduced ring is reduced: if $(x/t)^n=0$, some denominator $u$ satisfies $ux^n=0$; then $(ux)^n=0$, so $ux=0$ and $x/t=0$. Thus $B\otimes_LH$ is reduced, proving (2).

source.place: Tag 0384, forward implication, written on affine local rings; Tag 035W and algebra.tex Tag 00DK.

proof.text: Assume (2), fix a finite purely inseparable extension $E/k$, and set $C=A\otimes_kE$. The map $A\to C$ is faithfully flat by [lem-weil-pbc-field-extension-base-change-faithfully-flat], hence injective by [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-universally-injective], applied with the module $N=A$ and $A\otimes_AC\cong C$. In characteristic $p>0$, the $A$-algebra $C$ is generated by $1\otimes e$ for $e\in E$. By [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension], each such generator has a $p^n$-th power in $A$; increase $n$ if necessary to have $n>0$. Also $p^n(1\otimes e)=0$. The injective map has nilpotent kernel, so [lem-pur-power-generated-spectrum-homeomorphism] applies and makes contraction $\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ a homeomorphism. In characteristic zero $E=k$, so the same conclusion holds by the identity. A homeomorphism preserves the specialization order (closures of points); maximal prime ideals are its maximal elements under inclusion. Since $A$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak pA$, $C$ is local and its unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$ is the unique prime contracting to $\mathfrak m$. This argument uses no Noetherian hypothesis.

source.place: Tags 035W and 0384, unique point after purely inseparable extension; algebra.tex Tag 0BRA.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-common-extension-fields], choose a field $F$ and compatible $k$-embeddings $L\to F$ and $E\to F$. Put $T=R\otimes_kF$. The isomorphism $S\otimes_LF\cong T$, $(r\otimes l)\otimes f\mapsto r\otimes lf$, with inverse $r\otimes f\mapsto(r\otimes1)\otimes f$, is [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-cancel-base-change] after swapping factors. Therefore $S\to T$ is faithfully flat by [lem-weil-pbc-field-extension-base-change-faithfully-flat]. By [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-surjective-spectrum] there is a prime $\mathfrak Q\subset T$ contracting to $\mathfrak q\subset S$. Put $D=T_{\mathfrak Q}$. Its contracted prime in $R$ is $\mathfrak p$, because the two field embeddings agree on $k$.

source.place: Tag 0384, choose a common field extension and a point above the prescribed upstairs point; fields.tex Tag 0H7K.

proof.text: Condition (2) applied to $F/L$ makes $B\otimes_LF$ reduced. By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-cancel-base-change], $B\otimes_LF\cong B\otimes_S(S\otimes_LF)$, $b\otimes f\mapsto b\otimes(1\otimes f)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-base-change] and the isomorphism $S\otimes_LF\cong T$ of step 3, this is the localization of $T$ at the image of $S\setminus\mathfrak q$. All those elements lie outside $\mathfrak Q$, so $D=T_{\mathfrak Q}$ is a further localization of $B\otimes_LF$. Explicitly a fraction $t/u$ in the first localization maps to the same fraction in $T_{\mathfrak Q}$; localizing further at all images of $t\notin\mathfrak Q$ gives every fraction in $D$ and the same equality relation. Thus $D$ is reduced by the nilpotent-fraction calculation of step 1.

source.place: Tag 0384, the local ring at the common-extension point is reduced.

proof.text: Let $R_E=R\otimes_kE$ and let $\mathfrak P$ be the inverse image of $\mathfrak Q$ under $R_E\to T$. Its contraction to $R$ is $\mathfrak p$. By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-cancel-base-change], $C=A\otimes_kE\cong A\otimes_R R_E$, $a\otimes e\mapsto a\otimes(1\otimes e)$; by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-base-change], $C$ is the localization of $R_E$ at the images of $V=R\setminus\mathfrak p$. Since these images avoid $\mathfrak P$, it gives a prime $\mathfrak P_C$ of $C$, consisting of fractions whose numerator belongs to $\mathfrak P$. It contracts to $\mathfrak m$ in $A$: a fraction $r/v\in A$ maps into it exactly when $r\in\mathfrak p$. Step 2 now gives $\mathfrak P_C=\mathfrak n$. Hence every element of $R_E\setminus\mathfrak P$ is a unit in $C$. The fraction map $(R_E)_{\mathfrak P}\to C$, $t/u\mapsto(t/1)(u/1)^{-1}$, is inverse to the localization map $C\to(R_E)_{\mathfrak P}$: both composites fix $R_E$ and all inverted denominators. Thus $(R_E)_{\mathfrak P}\cong C$, compatibly with the maps to $D$.

source.place: Tags 035W and 0384, identify the finite purely inseparable local ring with the unlocalized scalar extension.

proof.text: The map $R_E\to T$ is faithfully flat: apply [lem-weil-pbc-field-extension-base-change-faithfully-flat] to the field extension $F/E$, and use [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-cancel-base-change] to identify $(R\otimes_kE)\otimes_EF$ with $R\otimes_kF$. In particular it is flat by [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-ring-maps] to $\mathfrak Q$ and its contraction $\mathfrak P$. It gives a flat local map $(R_E)_{\mathfrak P}\to T_{\mathfrak Q}$. Under step 5 this is a flat local map $C\to D$ between local rings, so [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-hom-faithfully-flat] makes it faithfully flat.

source.place: Tag 0384, the comparison of local rings is flat local and therefore faithfully flat; algebra.tex Tags 00HT and 00HR.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-universally-injective] to $C\to D$ with $N=C$, identifying $C\otimes_CD$ with $D$. Thus $C\to D$ is injective. If $z^n=0$ in $C$, its image is nilpotent in the reduced ring $D$, hence zero, and injectivity gives $z=0$. Therefore $C=A\otimes_kE$ is reduced for every finite purely inseparable $E/k$, including $E=k$.

source.place: Tag 0384, reducedness descends along the faithfully flat local comparison; algebra.tex Tags 033F (lemma-descent-reduced) and 05CK.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-geometric-reducedness-finite-inseparable-test] to the commutative $k$-algebra $A$. Step 7 verifies its finite purely inseparable condition, so $A\otimes_kK$ is reduced for every extension field $K/k$. This is (1), completing the reverse implication and the equivalence.

source.place: Tag 0384, final finite purely inseparable test, via Tag 035W and algebra.tex Tag 030V.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0384, lemma-geometrically-reduced-upstairs, expressed directly in affine local rings as in Tag 035W; the finite purely inseparable test is algebra.tex Tag 030V.
